To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the volume of activation during the application of a newly learned category is initially increased and then decreased as learning progresses.
the magnitude of the reduction in activation correlates with each individual's rate of learning and that the magnitude of this reduction is dependent upon the materials used during training.
the magnitude of reductions in activation with improvements in performance correlates with the magnitude of the initial increase in activation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of cortical activation patterns during the application of a newly learned category.
the functional anatomy of the brain as it learns new categories.
the neural mechanisms underlying the acquisition of new categories.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there are at least two stages involved in the use of a category.
the brain learns to do things more efficiently.
the brain is a very complex organ, and that it is not yet possible to understand how the various parts of the brain interact to produce a given function, such as language or vision.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the brain is a dynamic system, and that the dynamics are a function of both learning and task performance.
the brain is not a fixed system, rather, it changes in response to the demands that are placed upon it.
the brain's initial response to a new task involves the recruitment of nearby tissue.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are two stages of activation during learning.
there are two distinct stages to the development of a new category.
fMRI can be used as a tool to characterize the variability observed across individuals during the early stages learning.
